title: Contributing to fpCompare
text: Fork package clone onto computer. haven’t done , recommend using usethis::create_from_github("PredictiveEcology/fpCompare", fork = TRUE). Install development dependencies devtools::install_dev_deps(), make sure package passes R CMD check running devtools::check(). R CMD check doesn’t pass cleanly, ’s good idea ask help continuing. Create Git branch pull request (PR). recommend using usethis::pr_init("brief-description--change"). Make changes, commit git, create PR running usethis::pr_push(), following prompts browser. title PR briefly describe change. body PR contain Fixes #issue-number. user-facing changes, add bullet top NEWS.md (.e. just first header). Follow style described https://style.tidyverse.org/news.html.

what: Reliable comparison of floating point numbers
title: fpCompare: reliable comparison of floating point numbers
text: Comparisons floating point numbers problematic due errors associated binary representation decimal numbers. Computer scientists programmers aware problems (.e.g., Goldberg 1991) yet people still use numerical methods fail account floating point errors (pitfall first highlighted First Circle “R Inferno” (Burns 2012)). avoid numerical rounding issues, R’s help file relational operators (e.g., ?'>') suggests using identical .equal making numerical comparisons: Inspired R FAQ 7.31 Stack Overflow answer, package provides new relational operators useful performing floating point number comparisons set tolerance: functions use base relational operators make comparisons, incorporate tolerance value (fpCompare.tolerance) similar .equal. default fpCompare.tolerance value .Machine$double.eps^0.5, set via options. default used .equal numeric comparisons.
code: x1 <- 0.5 - 0.3 x2 <- 0.3 - 0.1 x1 == x2                           ## FALSE on most machines identical(all.equal(x1, x2), TRUE) ## TRUE everywhere ## set tolerance value tol <- .Machine$double.eps^0.5     ## default value options(fpCompare.tolerance = tol)  ## perform comparisons x1 <- 0.5 - 0.3 x2 <- 0.3 - 0.1 x1 == x2         ## FALSE on most machines x1 %==% x2       ## TRUE everywhere
